tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.why: A voice change is a tenant change. Identity, domain, and admin role decide whether the later work can exist.
tracks.outcome: You can name the tenant boundary, the account types, and the admin roles before anyone mentions an SBC.

chart.title: Identity before dial tone
chart.note: Order of operations, not a volume.

tracks.title: Licensing
tracks.why: The wrong SKU looks like a routing bug. Teams Phone, Calling Plans, Audio Conferencing, resource accounts, and Teams Premium are different purchases.
tracks.outcome: You can pick a license set for a user, a room, and a voice app, and say what Teams Premium does not include.

chart.title: Separate purchases
chart.note: Each bar is a distinct license family, not a price.

tracks.title: PowerShell and admin
tracks.why: The portal hides order. The shell shows the object you actually changed, and it is how compliance recording is assigned.
tracks.outcome: You can read a user, name the cmdlet family, and refuse to guess parameters you have not checked.

chart.title: Read, then change
chart.note: Sequence of a safe change.

tracks.title: Network and QoS
tracks.why: Teams audio dies in the same queues as file copies unless the path is short and the mark survives.
tracks.outcome: You can recite the port and DSCP table and say why a VPN is not a media design.

chart.title: DSCP values from the QoS article
chart.note: Bar length is the DSCP mark, not a traffic volume.

tracks.title: PSTN connectivity
tracks.why: Every external call uses one of four connectivity options. Mixing them is allowed. Pretending they are the same license is not.
tracks.outcome: You can choose Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, or Direct Routing for a specific user population.

chart.title: Who carries the call
chart.note: Teaching weight of how much you operate.

tracks.title: Routing and dial plans
tracks.why: Normalization and routing are two steps. A number that is not E.164 never gets a fair chance at a voice route.
tracks.outcome: You can walk usages in order, apply first-match normalization, and explain Islands mode.

chart.title: First match, then route
chart.note: Teaching sequence.

tracks.title: Attendants and queues
tracks.why: The number people publish is often a voice app, not a human. The resource account is the identity of that app.
tracks.outcome: You can design an attendant, a queue, overflow, and the license on the resource account.

chart.title: Voice app, not a user
chart.note: Required objects.

tracks.title: Emergency, LBR, survivability
tracks.why: Emergency calling is a design gate, not a checkbox after go-live. Location-based routing and branch survivability use the same network map.
tracks.outcome: You can explain dynamic location, who routes a Direct Routing emergency call, and what an SBA is for.

chart.title: Location before the carrier
chart.note: Teaching sequence for a site.

tracks.title: Devices and media
tracks.why: Phones, rooms, and media bypass change where RTP flows. Signaling still belongs to Teams.
tracks.outcome: You can decide bypass versus the media processor and license a room without inventing a Calling Plan.

chart.title: Two media paths
chart.note: Path choice, not a quality score.

tracks.title: Session border controllers
tracks.why: Microsoft supports Direct Routing on certified SBCs. AudioCodes, Ribbon, Oracle, and Cisco CUBE are families you will meet. The support path starts with the vendor.
tracks.outcome: You can say what certification buys, and what you still configure on each family.

chart.title: Certified or unsupported
chart.note: Shared gate, then vendor detail.

tracks.title: TLS, certificates, SIP
tracks.why: A dial-plan argument is wasted when the certificate name is wrong. OPTIONS tell you the trunk is alive.
tracks.outcome: You can walk a TLS failure, the three SIP proxies, and the codec list including the AMR-WB bypass limit.

chart.title: Handshake before INVITE
chart.note: Failure order.

tracks.title: Troubleshooting
tracks.why: Call Analytics is one call. CQD is a building. The SBC trace is the ladder. Mixing them up wastes the hour.
tracks.outcome: You can pick the tool that matches the scope of the fault and name one hypothesis.

chart.title: Scope the evidence
chart.note: Which tool, not a made-up rate.

tracks.title: Dynamics contact center
tracks.why: Dynamics 365 Contact Center is Microsoft’s CCaaS. Unified routing, channels, and Copilot are the job, and AB-250 is the exam that matches it.
tracks.outcome: You can name workstreams, queues, capacity, and the published AB-250 skill weights.

chart.title: AB-250 skill weights, low end of the published range
chart.note: Study guide accessed 14 October 2026. Ranges are wider than the bar.

tracks.title: Coexistence and CCaaS
tracks.why: Connect, Extend, and Unify are different media paths. CUCM, Webex, UCCE, Genesys, and Amazon Connect each need a named bridge, not a slogan.
tracks.outcome: You can say which model a design is, and where CUBE sits between CUCM and Teams.

chart.title: Three models on Learn
chart.note: Current names as of 14 October 2026.

tracks.title: ACS, Speech, Copilot
tracks.why: Call Automation is a server-side call with events. Speech and Copilot Studio can sit in the recognize step. Foundry is where you evaluate a model, not a second phone system.
tracks.outcome: You can sketch answer, play, recognize, and transfer, with a human escape.

chart.title: IVR as events
chart.note: Teaching sequence of one call.

tracks.title: Certifications and status
tracks.why: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta.
tracks.outcome: You can correct a retired exam number without bluffing a replacement.

chart.title: Status on 14 October 2026
chart.note: 3 means a live target, 2 means in beta, 1 means retired. Not a difficulty score.

tracks.title: Ecosystem
tracks.why: Glossary, mind map, sister technologies, integration maps, bridges, and future hooks.
tracks.outcome: You can draw the mind map, configure a compliance-recording gate, and say which identifier joins the logs.

chart.title: Sister systems
chart.note: Each bar is a system that must not be confused with Teams Phone itself.

tracks.title: CRM and CTI
tracks.why: Dynamics 365 voice and Salesforce Voice each document a bridge from the call to the CRM record.
tracks.outcome: You can say which app notifies the representative, and which identifier should join the call to the record.

chart.title: Bridge order
chart.note: Teaching sequence. Not a customer count.

tracks.title: Comparison
tracks.why: Microsoft, Amazon Connect Customer, and Google CCAI, described only from pages this lab opened.
tracks.outcome: You can name the product as the opened page names it, and you can say what those pages do not decide.

chart.title: Pages opened
chart.note: Each bar means a page was opened. Length is not a rank.

tracks.title: Routing, WFM, QM
tracks.why: Unified routing assigns work. Workforce management forecasts it. Quality evaluation scores it.
tracks.outcome: You can separate classification, assignment, a forecast, and a quality plan, and say which control failed.

chart.title: Three controls
chart.note: Teaching order. Not a staffing target.

lessonIndex.title: The tenant boundary
lessonIndex.say: Name the tenant, the verified domain, and that onmicrosoft.com cannot be the SBC name.

lessonIndex.title: Entra ID accounts voice will use
lessonIndex.say: Resource accounts do not sign in. Humans and rooms do.

lessonIndex.title: Roles that can change voice
lessonIndex.say: I will use a telephony or Teams admin role, not a shared global admin.

lessonIndex.title: The admin-center map
lessonIndex.say: Licenses in one center, voice objects in the other, effective policy from the shell.

lessonIndex.title: Exchange and Cloud Voicemail
lessonIndex.say: Cloud Voicemail needs a mailbox. The SBC cannot store the message for you.

lessonIndex.title: What homed online means
lessonIndex.say: Direct Routing users are homed online, and they are not in Islands mode.

lessonIndex.title: The license stack
lessonIndex.say: Teams Phone is not a carrier. Name the connectivity option separately.

lessonIndex.title: Calling Plan flavors
lessonIndex.say: Calling Plans are Microsoft as the carrier, sold only in some countries, in three usual flavors.

lessonIndex.title: Teams Premium is not PSTN
lessonIndex.say: Teams Premium does not include a phone system or a carrier.

lessonIndex.title: Resource account licenses
lessonIndex.say: Resource accounts get the Teams Phone Resource Account license, not Teams Phone Standard.

lessonIndex.title: Rooms, common area, and shared calling
lessonIndex.say: A Direct Routing common-area phone does not need a Calling Plan. A room has its own SKU.

lessonIndex.title: A license set you can defend
lessonIndex.say: I separate Teams Phone, the carrier, Audio Conferencing, the resource account, and Premium.

lessonIndex.title: The module and the session
lessonIndex.say: I connect the MicrosoftTeams module to a named tenant and read help before I change anything.

lessonIndex.title: Objects you will actually get
lessonIndex.say: Usage, route, policy, gateway. The policy is what the user has. The route is what the pattern does.

lessonIndex.title: Grant, set, and new
lessonIndex.say: Grant assigns to a user. Set changes an object. I read both times.

lessonIndex.title: Reading a user before you change one
lessonIndex.say: I read the effective policy with Get-CsOnlineUser before I edit anything.

lessonIndex.title: When the portal and the shell disagree
lessonIndex.say: I will trust a fresh Get- over a stale toast, then place one test call.

lessonIndex.title: Safety on a lab tenant
lessonIndex.say: I will not discover certificate behavior on the company trunk.

lessonIndex.title: Shortest path, no media proxy
lessonIndex.say: Local egress, no media proxy, ExpressRoute not required.

lessonIndex.title: The port and DSCP table
lessonIndex.say: Audio is 46 on ports 50000 to 50019. I can place the other three without a card.

lessonIndex.title: VPN and the split tunnel
lessonIndex.say: I keep real-time media off the full-tunnel VPN, and I do not label the VPN pool as HQ.

lessonIndex.title: Bandwidth you can calculate
lessonIndex.say: G.711 at 20 ms is 80 kbit/s at layer 3 and 87.2 with a typical Ethernet header.

lessonIndex.title: Proving the mark survived
lessonIndex.say: I capture at the egress and show DSCP 46 still on the audio ports.

lessonIndex.title: ExpressRoute is not the requirement
lessonIndex.say: Teams does not require ExpressRoute. Local internet egress is the normal plan.

lessonIndex.title: Four ways to reach the PSTN
lessonIndex.say: Four options. Microsoft is the carrier only for Calling Plans. Mixing them in one tenant is allowed.

lessonIndex.title: Calling Plans in practice
lessonIndex.say: Calling Plan users should not inherit a Direct Routing route by accident.

lessonIndex.title: Operator Connect
lessonIndex.say: Operator Connect is Teams Phone plus a certified carrier. I do not also build an SBC for those same numbers.

lessonIndex.title: Teams Phone Mobile
lessonIndex.say: Teams Phone Mobile makes the SIM number the Teams number. I would not put a queue on it.

lessonIndex.title: Direct Routing
lessonIndex.say: 5061 to the three commercial proxies, media on those UDP ranges, certificate name matches the FQDN, user has a route.

lessonIndex.title: Mixing them in one tenant
lessonIndex.say: I mix options on purpose, with a policy per population.

lessonIndex.title: Normalize, then route
lessonIndex.say: First matching normalization rule wins. I test the route with the normalized number.

lessonIndex.title: Dial plans and first match
lessonIndex.say: Specific rules first, grant the plan to the user, test as that user.

lessonIndex.title: PSTN usages are the permission
lessonIndex.say: The usage is the permission. The policy is the ordered list of permissions on the user.

lessonIndex.title: Voice routes and gateways
lessonIndex.say: The voice route is a regex and a gateway list. I rehearse failover.

lessonIndex.title: A London worked example
lessonIndex.say: I can walk one number through normalize, usage, route, and gateway.

lessonIndex.title: Islands mode and other hard stops
lessonIndex.say: I list the hard stops before I tune a regex.

lessonIndex.title: Resource accounts for voice apps
lessonIndex.say: The resource account is the voice app’s identity. The number is optional until you publish it.

lessonIndex.title: Auto attendant design
lessonIndex.say: Hours, holidays, greeting, scoped directory, and an operator. Every key has a target.

lessonIndex.title: Queue routing methods
lessonIndex.say: I can define the four routing methods and I will test presence with two agents.

lessonIndex.title: Timeout, overflow, and outbound funding
lessonIndex.say: Overflow is a target I have tested. External overflow is funded.

lessonIndex.title: Nested voice apps
lessonIndex.say: One pilot number, a drawn tree, no loops, overflow that ends.

lessonIndex.title: Numbers on voice apps
lessonIndex.say: Service numbers sit on resource accounts. Caller ID is a choice.

lessonIndex.title: Emergency calling is a design gate
lessonIndex.say: Emergency is a gate. I will not demo a bot on the emergency number.

lessonIndex.title: Dynamic location
lessonIndex.say: Trusted IP, subnet, civic address. The VPN pool is not headquarters.

lessonIndex.title: Calling Plans versus Direct Routing emergency
lessonIndex.say: Calling Plan emergency and Direct Routing emergency are different owners. I will not copy one route onto the other.

lessonIndex.title: Location-based routing
lessonIndex.say: LBR keeps PSTN in-country. I will re-read it before I enable media bypass there.

lessonIndex.title: Survivable Branch Appliance
lessonIndex.say: SBA is local PSTN survivability for Direct Routing, not a full Teams cloud.

lessonIndex.title: Notification and the test call
lessonIndex.say: I test emergency with the carrier’s process and I check that on-site notification fired.

lessonIndex.title: Certified phones
lessonIndex.say: I buy from the current certified list, or I use SIP Gateway for the devices it actually supports.

lessonIndex.title: Teams Rooms
lessonIndex.say: Rooms get a room license and a Conditional Access exception you can explain.

lessonIndex.title: SIP Gateway and analog
lessonIndex.say: Analog stays on the SBC or SIP Gateway, with an emergency test from that device.

lessonIndex.title: Media bypass
lessonIndex.say: Bypass is media only. SIP still goes through Teams. I check LBR and the VPN first.

lessonIndex.title: Local media optimization
lessonIndex.say: Local media optimization is about which SBC interface the media uses. I will draw both.

lessonIndex.title: Common area phones, again, as devices
lessonIndex.say: A common-area phone has its own account. I will not sign it in as a person who left.

lessonIndex.title: What certification buys you
lessonIndex.say: Certification is a release on Microsoft’s list. Support starts with the vendor.

lessonIndex.title: AudioCodes pattern
lessonIndex.say: I follow AudioCodes’ current guide for the firmware, and I still check the shared gate.

lessonIndex.title: Ribbon pattern
lessonIndex.say: I confirm the Ribbon release and the interface that answers OPTIONS.

lessonIndex.title: Oracle Communications SBC
lessonIndex.say: I match the Oracle release to the certified list before I praise the config.

lessonIndex.title: Cisco CUBE for Teams
lessonIndex.say: CUBE is a certified SBC with dial-peers in two directions and early offer toward Teams.

lessonIndex.title: The support boundary
lessonIndex.say: Vendor first, with firmware and a Call-ID. I keep the certified-list date.

lessonIndex.title: The certificate profile
lessonIndex.say: Public CA, SAN matches the paired FQDN, server EKU, TLS 1.2 or newer.

lessonIndex.title: Names, wildcards, and the paired FQDN
lessonIndex.say: The certificate name, the DNS name, and the paired FQDN are the same name.

lessonIndex.title: Three SIP proxies and failover
lessonIndex.say: Three commercial proxies, government clouds have their own names, firewall the ranges.

lessonIndex.title: SIP OPTIONS
lessonIndex.say: I treat missed OPTIONS as a trunk problem and I look at the admin-center status beside the SBC log.

lessonIndex.title: Codecs and SRTP
lessonIndex.say: I offer G.711, I use SRTP, and I test DTMF through the carrier.

lessonIndex.title: Failover you can rehearse
lessonIndex.say: I rehearse failover and I know the certificate expiry date.

lessonIndex.title: One hypothesis
lessonIndex.say: One hypothesis, one change, one evidence pack.

lessonIndex.title: Reading a ladder
lessonIndex.say: I read the first failing response on one Call-ID.

lessonIndex.title: Call Analytics
lessonIndex.say: Call Analytics is one call. I will not use it to explain a subnet.

lessonIndex.title: Call Quality Dashboard
lessonIndex.say: I split loss, jitter, and RTT, and I trust CQD only after I trust the subnet map.

lessonIndex.title: Trunk health
lessonIndex.say: I check TLS and OPTIONS before I touch a normalization rule.

lessonIndex.title: A fault catalog
lessonIndex.say: I can sort a symptom into signaling, media, policy, or location before I pick a tool.

lessonIndex.title: Customer Service and Contact Center
lessonIndex.say: Contact Center is the CCaaS. A Teams auto attendant is not. AB-250 is the exam. MB-280 is retired and was the wrong scope anyway.

lessonIndex.title: Channels
lessonIndex.say: Channels are the largest AB-250 slice. I will not only study Copilot.

lessonIndex.title: Unified routing
lessonIndex.say: Workstream, classification, queue, assignment. Unknown intent has a human default.

lessonIndex.title: Representative experience and Copilot
lessonIndex.say: Copilot assists the representative. It is not the route, and its sources have to be true.

lessonIndex.title: Voice on ACS
lessonIndex.say: Contact Center voice runs on ACS. Teams Phone extensibility is how you avoid a second phone, when the design is actually certified for it.

lessonIndex.title: The AB-250 map
lessonIndex.say: AB-250, 700 to pass, channels are the biggest slice, MB-280 practice tests are the wrong pile.

lessonIndex.title: Connect, Extend, and Unify
lessonIndex.say: I use Connect, Extend, and Unify. If someone says Power, I ask which current model they mean.

lessonIndex.title: Teams Phone extensibility
lessonIndex.say: Extensibility reuses Teams Phone. I want the vendor’s current certification, not only a presence sync.

lessonIndex.title: CUCM and CUBE
lessonIndex.say: One normalization owner. Tromboning is temporary. Rollback keeps the old trunk.

lessonIndex.title: Webex calling interop
lessonIndex.say: Webex voice interop is a SIP bridge and a numbering plan, not a chat project.

lessonIndex.title: UCCE during a move
lessonIndex.say: I do not put UCCE agents on Teams and expect CVP to keep controlling them.

lessonIndex.title: Genesys and Amazon Connect
lessonIndex.say: I ask Genesys which model, and I draw the SIP path for Amazon Connect. I store a Call-ID either way.

lessonIndex.title: Calling SDK versus Call Automation
lessonIndex.say: Call Automation is the server-side IVR. The Calling SDK is a person in the browser.

lessonIndex.title: Teams interop from ACS
lessonIndex.say: ACS does not automatically become a Teams user. I follow the interop article and I test the transfer.

lessonIndex.title: An IVR as events
lessonIndex.say: Answer, play, recognize, transfer. The escape is tested every time the prompt changes.

lessonIndex.title: Azure AI Speech
lessonIndex.say: I pick a voice I am allowed to use, match the language, and log what the recognizer heard.

lessonIndex.title: Copilot Studio voice
lessonIndex.say: The voice agent has sources I trust and an escape I tested. It does not own emergency calls.

lessonIndex.title: Foundry, and what not to invent
lessonIndex.say: I evaluate the model before it touches a phone number, and I do not design around unannounced features.

lessonIndex.title: MS-700 on 14 October 2026
lessonIndex.say: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.

lessonIndex.title: MB-280, AB-210, and AB-250
lessonIndex.say: MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. AB-250 is the contact-center exam.

lessonIndex.title: AZ-900 and SC-900
lessonIndex.say: AZ-900 and SC-900 are context. MS-900 and AI-900 are retired. The role exams still matter.

lessonIndex.title: Learning paths that match the job
lessonIndex.say: I study foundations, then the phone system, then the contact center. I re-read Learn when I am about to change production.

lessonIndex.title: The status board
lessonIndex.say: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta.

lessonIndex.title: How to use the readiness map
lessonIndex.say: A readiness score is mine, in this browser, and the study guide still wins.

lessonIndex.title: Voice is not a closed box
lessonIndex.say: I can name the sister system and the identifier that joins it to the call.

lessonIndex.title: How to use the glossary
lessonIndex.say: I can define the term, the fault, and the document I would open.

lessonIndex.title: The mind map
lessonIndex.say: I can draw Teams, the SBC, the carrier, and the six sister systems without notes.

lessonIndex.title: Compliance recording and quality management
lessonIndex.say: Compliance recording is a partner bot, a policy, and an application instance. Users do not start it. I test a new call.

lessonIndex.title: Workforce management
lessonIndex.say: I staff from queue intervals, Erlang C, and an explicit shrinkage. I do not staff from Call Analytics.

lessonIndex.title: E911 as a system of record
lessonIndex.say: One subnet list feeds emergency location, LBR, and CQD. I can say which consumer is wrong when they disagree.

lessonIndex.title: Analytics and Power BI
lessonIndex.say: Power BI comes after the grain is right. I will not show a VPN pool as headquarters.

lessonIndex.title: CRM and screen pop
lessonIndex.say: Screen pop needs E.164 and should write the Call-ID. Teams alone does not open the case.

lessonIndex.title: AI agents beside the queue
lessonIndex.say: The agent has a tested escape and a staffed overflow. It is not the emergency route.

lessonIndex.title: Integration maps
lessonIndex.say: I start from the goal and list the systems, including the identifier.

lessonIndex.title: Cross-platform bridges
lessonIndex.say: A cross-platform voice bridge is an SBC, one normalizer, written ranges, and a rollback.

lessonIndex.title: Future-integration hooks
lessonIndex.say: I can name the seams I am leaving, and the failure if I skip one. I am not promising an unannounced product.

lessonIndex.title: Configuring an ecosystem change
lessonIndex.say: My change list names the sisters, not only the SBC.

lessonIndex.title: Troubleshooting across a vendor boundary
lessonIndex.say: I name the boundary and the join key before I ask a vendor to change anything.

lessonIndex.title: What CTI names
lessonIndex.say: CTI names the coordination. The vendor page names the product.

lessonIndex.title: The Dynamics voice channel
lessonIndex.say: The voice channel is ACS calling inside Dynamics, routed like the other channels.

lessonIndex.title: Teams Phone into the voice channel
lessonIndex.say: Teams can carry the number. A Calling Plan here is service numbers only.

lessonIndex.title: The resource account and the number
lessonIndex.say: I sync the Teams service number, and the representative answers in Copilot Service workspace.

lessonIndex.title: Salesforce Voice and Partner Contact Center
lessonIndex.say: Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice, and the help page places it in Partner Contact Center.

lessonIndex.title: Amazon Connect and partner telephony
lessonIndex.say: I can point at which Salesforce telephony path the learning map names.

lessonIndex.title: The call-to-record seam
lessonIndex.say: I name the desktop that answers, and the identifier that joins the call to the record.

lessonIndex.title: A comparison with no winner
lessonIndex.say: I can cite the page, and I will not rank the vendors.

lessonIndex.title: What the Microsoft pages name
lessonIndex.say: I can say which Microsoft article I am quoting before I name a model.

lessonIndex.title: Amazon Connect Customer
lessonIndex.say: The guide I opened calls the contact-center product Amazon Connect Customer.

lessonIndex.title: CCAI Platform and the GECX rename
lessonIndex.say: The docs page still says Contact Center AI Platform. The change log records the GECX rename.

lessonIndex.title: Documented differences only
lessonIndex.say: I can fill the table from the pages and leave the score column off.

lessonIndex.title: What these pages do not decide
lessonIndex.say: I can say what this comparison refuses to decide.

lessonIndex.title: Classification, then assignment
lessonIndex.say: Classification adds information. Assignment uses it. They are not the same stage.

lessonIndex.title: Voice workstreams and voice queues
lessonIndex.say: A voice workstream is push only. I will not edit that mode later, because the page says I cannot.

lessonIndex.title: Highest capacity, round robin, least active
lessonIndex.say: I can name which assignment method the queue uses, and I will not use it to rank employees.

lessonIndex.title: Forecast, capacity, and schedule
lessonIndex.say: Forecast volume and handle time, then capacity, then shifts. The short-term horizon on the page is up to 42 days.

lessonIndex.title: Indicators and guardrails
lessonIndex.say: An indicator scores. A guardrail flags a required or prohibited behavior. Neither one is an employment decision.

lessonIndex.title: Two recording controls
lessonIndex.say: I will check the Dynamics announcement and the Teams recording policy as two controls.

lessonIndex.title: Which control failed
lessonIndex.say: I name the control that failed before I change a different one.

scenarios.title: The trunk that is not a trunk
scenarios.brief: A London pilot cannot dial out. The SBC shows a TLS alert. Someone wants to rewrite the dial plan.
choices: Rewrite the UK normalization rules.
Check the certificate name, expiry, and chain against the paired FQDN.
Buy Teams Premium for the pilot users.
Move the users to Islands mode.
scenarios.debrief: SIP never starts when TLS fails. The dial plan is innocent until OPTIONS succeed. Teams Premium does not repair a certificate, and Islands mode is unsupported for Direct Routing.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Silence after 200 OK
scenarios.brief: INVITE completes with 200 OK and ACK. Neither side hears audio. Signaling ports are open.
scenarios.prompt: What is the most likely gap?
choices: The dial plan stripped a digit.
Media UDP ranges between the SBC and the media processors are closed, or SRTP is stripped.
The user needs Audio Conferencing.
CQD has not been installed on the PC.
scenarios.debrief: A completed INVITE means signaling worked. Direct Routing media uses UDP 3478–3481 and 49152–53247 unless bypass keeps media off that path, and media is SRTP.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: onmicrosoft.com
scenarios.brief: The only domain in the tenant is contoso.onmicrosoft.com. The design names the SBC sbc.contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
scenarios.prompt: What do you tell the project?
choices: That name is the recommended Direct Routing FQDN.
Verify a real domain and use an FQDN on it. onmicrosoft.com is not eligible.
Operator Connect requires that name.
Call the emergency test number to prove it.
scenarios.debrief: The plan page says the SBC FQDN must belong to a verified domain and shows onmicrosoft.com as not supported.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Premium instead of a Calling Plan
scenarios.brief: Procurement removed Calling Plans because Teams Premium was added. Users must dial the PSTN through Microsoft as the carrier.
choices: Nothing. Premium includes PSTN.
Teams Phone if it is not already there, plus a Calling Plan. Premium does not replace either.
Only a resource account license.
scenarios.debrief: Teams Premium is a meetings add-on. Calling Plans are the Microsoft-operated PSTN license on top of Teams Phone.
scenarios.source: Teams add-on licensing and Calling Plans articles, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Resource account swap
scenarios.brief: A queue stopped the morning after an admin removed Teams Phone Standard, saved, then later added the Teams Phone Resource Account license.
scenarios.prompt: What does Microsoft tell you to do differently?
choices: Assign Teams Phone Standard again. It is the right SKU.
Swap in one license change. If the app is already broken, create a new resource account on the correct license.
Delete the dial plan.
Enable Islands mode on the resource account.
scenarios.debrief: The resource-account license article says to remove Standard and add the resource-account license in the same change, and warns that a two-step swap can break the voice app.
scenarios.source: Teams Phone Resource Account licenses, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: 999 and the catch-all
scenarios.brief: A normalization rule at the top matches any digits and prepends +44. Emergency 999 now looks like an ordinary UK number and takes the international gateway in another country.
choices: Emergency rules must be first, with a route that stays local.
999 should be left untranslated forever.
Media bypass will fix the destination.
Teams Premium includes emergency routing.
scenarios.debrief: First match wins. An emergency short code that is rewritten by a general rule never sees the emergency route. Direct Routing emergency egress is your SBC and carrier.
scenarios.source: Dial plans and emergency calling articles, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Branch can dial the US
scenarios.brief: A Manchester policy was copied from headquarters. Headquarters usages include international. Manchester was only supposed to dial the UK and emergency.
choices: The SBC firmware.
The branch policy still contains the international usage.
They need a Calling Plan and Direct Routing on the same user by accident.
CQD classification.
scenarios.debrief: The ordered PSTN usages on the policy are the permission. Copying a policy copies the permission.
scenarios.source: Voice routing policies, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Callback that never calls back
scenarios.brief: A queue offers callback. The greeting plays. No return call is placed. User Calling Plans are funded. The resource account is not.
choices: Agents need Teams Premium.
Callback is outbound from the resource account and needs pay-as-you-go or communications credits.
SIP OPTIONS are optional for callbacks.
The Ethernet header is too small.
scenarios.debrief: The voice-app prerequisite article treats callback as a case that needs funding on the resource account.
scenarios.source: Voice applications prerequisites and licensing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: VPN users at headquarters
scenarios.brief: Remote workers on a full-tunnel VPN show the HQ floor as their emergency address. CQD also paints their poor calls as HQ.
choices: Label the VPN pool as HQ so the map is simple.
Do not treat the VPN range as a dispatchable HQ site. Keep media off the full tunnel if you can.
Turn off emergency calling for VPN users.
Enable AMR-WB.
scenarios.debrief: Trusted IPs and subnets decide dynamic location. A VPN pool is not a floor. Microsoft also recommends keeping real-time media off a VPN.
scenarios.source: Emergency locations and QoS articles, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Bypass and a regulated site
scenarios.brief: Location-based routing is on for a site. A colleague enables media bypass so audio ‘takes the short path’ through an SBC in another country.
choices: Bypass never affects where media egresses.
Signaling always stays with Teams, and bypass must not create an illegal media egress. Read the LBR article before you enable it.
Bypass turns off the need for a certificate.
LBR only applies to chat.
scenarios.debrief: Media bypass changes the media path, not the SIP path. LBR exists to stop the wrong egress.
scenarios.source: Direct Routing plan and location-based routing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: 488 after a CUCM change
scenarios.brief: CUBE was inserted between CUCM and Teams. CUCM still sends delayed offer. Calls fail with 488.
choices: Teams Direct Routing expects early offer. Push delayed offer through and the SDP fails.
488 means the certificate expired.
488 means Islands mode.
You must assign Audio Conferencing to CUBE.
scenarios.debrief: The campus teaches early offer toward Teams as the CUBE pattern. 488 is an SDP refusal. Confirm the symptom in SDP before you rebuild the dial plan.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing and Cisco CUBE guidance for the release you run.

scenarios.title: Private CA in production
scenarios.brief: The lab trunk used an internal CA and worked against a simulator. Production pairing to sip.pstnhub fails the handshake.
choices: Production accepts private CAs if the SBC is certified.
The production certificate has to come from a CA in Microsoft’s trusted root program.
You should switch the FQDN to onmicrosoft.com.
TLS 1.0 is required.
scenarios.debrief: The plan page requires a certificate from a trusted public CA for the paired name.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: One angry caller, one red building
scenarios.brief: One executive had a bad call from home. Separately, a whole floor shows loss with DSCP 46 still present.
choices: CQD for the executive, Call Analytics for the floor.
Call Analytics for the executive, CQD for the floor.
SIP OPTIONS for both.
The Erlang calculator for both.
scenarios.debrief: Call Analytics is per user and per call. CQD is the aggregate. Loss with the mark intact points at the path, not at a missing DSCP policy.
scenarios.source: Call Analytics and CQD articles, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: French callers in the English queue
scenarios.brief: A Dynamics contact center workstream answers voice. French billing callers reach the general English queue.
choices: A Teams dial-plan rule that strips French country codes.
Classification that sets language and intent, and representatives who actually have that skill.
Teams Premium on the SBC.
Islands mode.
scenarios.debrief: Unified routing classifies the work item before assignment. Skills on a slide do not count.
scenarios.source: AB-250 study guide, work distribution and channels, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Power, the unlabeled model
scenarios.brief: A proposal says the contact center uses the Power model. Nobody can say whether media is an SBC, the Teams client, or ACS.
choices: A discount.
Which current Learn model it is: Connect, Extend, or Unify, plus the certification.
A Calling Plan for every agent regardless of model.
scenarios.debrief: Learn’s article on 14 October 2026 names Connect, Extend, and Unify. Older wording says Power. The model decides ports and licenses.
scenarios.source: Teams contact center article, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Transfer to an expert
scenarios.brief: A Connect-model contact center transfers callers to finance staff who only have Teams chat. The transfer fails.
scenarios.prompt: What does the Connect note imply?
choices: Finance needs Teams Phone and a number. The contact-center agent’s own license is a separate question.
Finance needs Islands mode.
Nobody needs a phone license for a PSTN transfer.
Replace the SBC with a glossary.
scenarios.debrief: Microsoft’s Connect description says the Teams user who receives a transfer needs a phone-system license and a number.
scenarios.source: Teams contact center, Connect model, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: The bot with no door
scenarios.brief: A Copilot Studio voice agent answers the public number. Callers who say ‘agent’ stay in the bot. Emergency numbers were also pointed at it.
choices: Add more generative topics and keep emergency on the bot.
Add a tested human escape, a staffed queue, and a separate emergency route that never hits the bot.
Disable TLS so digits are easier.
Assign AI-900.
scenarios.debrief: An IVR without an escape traps people. Emergency calling is a route and a location, not a topic.
scenarios.source: Copilot Studio and emergency calling docs, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Wrong exam, right job
scenarios.brief: A contact-center engineer is told to book MB-280 in October 2026, or AB-210 if MB-280 is awkward.
choices: Book MB-280. It is the contact-center exam.
MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. AB-250 is the contact-center exam. AB-210 does not replace MS-700.
Book MS-900.
Book AI-900.
scenarios.debrief: MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026, with AB-210 as its successor; AB-210 is in beta. AB-250 is the contact-center certification. AB-210 is not a replacement for MS-700.
scenarios.source: Learn retirement list, Partner Center July 2026, AB-250 study guide.

scenarios.title: MS-700 is dead, says a blog
scenarios.brief: A blog claims MS-700 was replaced and should not be studied. The candidate’s job is Teams administration, including voice.
choices: The undated blog.
MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.
AI-900, because voice is AI now.
scenarios.debrief: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement. Quote the check date. Re-read the guide after Oct 27 2026 before sitting it.
scenarios.source: MS-700 study guide and certification page, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Policy without a bot
scenarios.brief: Compliance recording policy is granted to traders. No application instance exists. A meeting that was already running shows no recorder.
scenarios.prompt: What do you tell the auditor?
choices: Granting the policy is enough, and existing meetings should have started recording.
The application instance is required, and existing calls are not swept in. Place a new test call after the bot is attached.
Turn on convenience recording and call it compliance.
Store the audio in the user’s mailbox by default.
scenarios.debrief: Learn says assignment alone does not activate recording without the application instance, and existing calls and meetings are unaffected. Compliance retention is the partner’s, not meeting storage.
scenarios.source: Compliance recording setup and New-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Overstaffed and overflowing
scenarios.brief: WFM says the queue had spare agents. Supervisors say almost every call overflowed. The export was one row per day.
scenarios.prompt: What is broken in the feed?
choices: Erlang C cannot be used on voice.
The interval is a day, so the busy half-hour is invisible, and overflow may have removed calls from this queue’s offered count.
DSCP 46 causes overflow.
They need a Calling Plan per agent to fix WFM.
scenarios.debrief: Workforce math needs the same interval the schedule uses. A daily total hides the peak. Overflow can also change the offered count.
scenarios.source: Teaching model beside Dynamics 365 Contact Center analytics.

scenarios.title: Wrong person pops
scenarios.brief: The CRM opens a contact for 02075554010 while the SBC trace shows +442075554010. Agents complain the screen is random.
choices: A fuzzy name match.
Normalize to E.164 before the lookup, and store the Call-ID on the case.
The Teams display name.
The DSCP value.
scenarios.debrief: Screen pop is only as good as the number you look up. Call-ID is what later joins the case to the ladder.
scenarios.source: Contact center and Direct Routing practice, accessed 14 October 2026.

scenarios.title: Double plus forty-four
scenarios.brief: During dual-running, CUCM translation adds +44 and the Teams dial plan also adds +44. The carrier rejects the number.
choices: Both sides should transform, for safety.
Pick one normalization owner and test both directions.
Remove TLS so the carrier can see the digits.
Enable media bypass to strip a plus.
scenarios.debrief: Coexistence fails when two systems both rewrite the called number. Tromboning may still happen. Double translation should not.
scenarios.source: Direct Routing plan and CUBE coexistence practice.

scenarios.title: Saturday certificate
scenarios.brief: The SBC certificate expires Saturday. The project plan has no date for it. OPTIONS are healthy on Friday.
choices: The Erlang shrinkage seam.
Certificate expiry is a monitored date. Healthy OPTIONS on Friday do not renew a certificate.
You need a new tenant.
Switch to AI-900.
scenarios.debrief: TLS fails the morning the certificate expires, and the symptom looks like a dead trunk. Calendar the date with the rest of the integration hooks.
scenarios.source: Plan Direct Routing, certificate requirements, accessed 14 October 2026.

faults.symptom: SBC pairing fails and the FQDN ends in onmicrosoft.com.
faults.cause: Direct Routing only pairs an FQDN on a verified domain. The default onmicrosoft.com domain is not eligible.
faults.fix: Add and verify the public domain, publish DNS, and pair that name.
faults.check: Get-CsOnlinePSTNGateway and the tenant's verified domains.

faults.symptom: Direct Routing is refused and the user is in Islands mode.
faults.cause: Direct Routing is not supported for users in Islands mode.
faults.fix: Move the user to Teams-only before you treat the SBC as the fault.
faults.check: Get-CsOnlineUser. Look at the coexistence mode.

faults.symptom: Outbound PSTN works for some users and fails for others on the same SBC.
faults.cause: Voice routing policies are per user. A missing usage or a policy that was never granted looks like a trunk failure.
faults.fix: Compare a working user and a failing user. Grant the policy that contains the usage.
faults.check: Get-CsOnlineUser voice policy fields, then the voice route pattern.

faults.symptom: The number leaves Teams as 10 digits and the carrier rejects it.
faults.cause: No normalization rule matched, so routing saw the raw digits.
faults.fix: Put a first-match rule that emits E.164 above any catch-all you do not trust.
faults.check: The dial plan effective for that user in the Teams client test.

faults.symptom: 999 reaches a national route instead of emergency.
faults.cause: A 10-digit or catch-all rule matched before the emergency rule, or the emergency usage is not first.
faults.fix: Emergency normalization and the emergency usage both go first.
faults.check: Trace 999 through the dial plan, then through the ordered usages.

faults.symptom: TLS fails with a name mismatch.
faults.cause: The certificate SAN does not contain the SBC FQDN paired in the tenant.
faults.fix: Reissue the certificate from a public CA in the Microsoft trusted root program, with server authentication EKU.
faults.check: The SBC handshake capture and Get-CsOnlinePSTNGateway FQDN.

faults.symptom: The trunk shows offline after a silent weekend.
faults.cause: The certificate expired, or OPTIONS stopped receiving 200 OK.
faults.fix: Renew on a calendar that is not the same week as the expiry. Restore OPTIONS.
faults.check: Certificate not-after date and the SBC OPTIONS log.

faults.symptom: Calls connect and then have no audio.
faults.cause: Signaling passed and media ports did not. A firewall allowed TCP 5061 and missed the UDP media range.
faults.fix: Open the current media ranges and budget at least two ports per concurrent call.
faults.check: SBC media capture. One-way RTP is a firewall or NAT symptom.

faults.symptom: Audio is fine on site and chopped on the VPN.
faults.cause: Real-time media is sharing a tunnel with bulk traffic, and the client source ports may not be marked.
faults.fix: Keep media off the VPN. Mark at the edge if the client cannot.
faults.check: CQD building view split by subnet, plus a Call Analytics row for one user.

faults.symptom: CQD shows a bad building and Call Analytics for one user looks clean.
faults.cause: You compared a population to a single call from a different hour.
faults.fix: Use Call Analytics for the one call and CQD for the subnet over the same days.
faults.check: CQD subnet report and the user's Call Analytics session.

faults.symptom: Every agent hears the call at once, including people already in a meeting.
faults.cause: The queue is attendant routing and presence-based routing is off, or presence is stale.
faults.fix: Turn on presence-based routing if the promise is to skip busy agents, and test with two accounts.
faults.check: Call queue routing method and a test call while one agent is in a meeting.

faults.symptom: The same agent gets every call.
faults.cause: Serial routing, and that person is first in the list.
faults.fix: Change the method or rotate the list on purpose.
faults.check: Get-CsCallQueue routing method and agent order.

faults.symptom: The auto attendant is silent after hours.
faults.cause: Business hours or the holiday set does not cover the time the caller used, or no greeting was uploaded.
faults.fix: Set hours, holidays, and an after-hours greeting. Call from outside those hours.
faults.check: Auto attendant call flow in the admin center, then a test call.

faults.symptom: The resource account will not take a phone number.
faults.cause: The license is missing, or Teams Phone Standard was assigned instead of the resource account license.
faults.fix: Swap to the Teams Phone Resource Account license in one change. Do not stack the user phone license.
faults.check: The license blade on that account. It should be disabled for sign-in.

faults.symptom: External transfer from the queue fails.
faults.cause: Outbound PSTN from a voice app needs pay-as-you-go or communications credits, and a path.
faults.fix: Fund the tenant and confirm the resource account may place the transfer.
faults.check: Voice app prerequisites. Place a test transfer to a non-production number.

faults.symptom: A Calling Plan user cannot get a dial-in conference number.
faults.cause: Audio Conferencing is a separate license.
faults.fix: Assign Audio Conferencing to the organizer, not a Calling Plan to the conference.
faults.check: The user's licenses, then a new meeting invite.

faults.symptom: Media bypass was enabled and AMR-WB calls fail.
faults.cause: AMR-WB is documented for non-bypass calls only.
faults.fix: Offer a shared codec that bypass allows, or turn bypass off for that path.
faults.check: SBC codec list and the bypass flag on the gateway.

faults.symptom: Location-based routing blocks a call that emergency routing should still place.
faults.cause: LBR and emergency are different designs that share the network map. A site mistake hits both.
faults.fix: Fix the site and subnet, then test emergency on a carrier test number and LBR on a toll call.
faults.check: Trusted IP, site, and subnet objects. Do not call a real emergency number.

faults.symptom: The branch dies when the WAN dies, including local PSTN.
faults.cause: There is no Survivable Branch Appliance, or clients cannot reach it.
faults.fix: Put an SBA on Direct Routing and prove local calls without Microsoft 365.
faults.check: SBA documentation for the firmware you run. Cloud features will still be down.

faults.symptom: Compliance recording policy is granted and nothing is recorded.
faults.cause: The policy has no application instance, or the policy is disabled, or the call started before the grant.
faults.fix: Create the application, attach it, enable the policy, grant it, and place a new call.
faults.check: Get-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy. Confirm the application and the users.

faults.symptom: Recorded calls have no retention when the meeting ends.
faults.cause: Compliance retention is the partner's, not Teams meeting storage.
faults.fix: Confirm the recorder's retention, export, and legal hold. Do not point auditors at meeting files.
faults.check: The partner portal for that Call-ID.

faults.symptom: A Teams user receives a contact-center transfer and cannot be reached.
faults.cause: In the Connect model the agent may not need a phone-system license, but the Teams user who receives the transfer does, plus a number.
faults.fix: License and number the transfer target. Keep the contact-center agents on the model you actually bought.
faults.check: Teams contact center article. The user's phone number assignment.

faults.symptom: The bot accepts an emergency call and never transfers.
faults.cause: The recognize step has no escape, and emergency must not sit behind a topic.
faults.fix: Route emergency before the bot. Give every other topic a human path.
faults.check: Call the test number. Confirm 999 or 911 never enters the topic.

faults.symptom: French callers land in an English billing queue.
faults.cause: The workstream classification does not include language, or the French queue has no capacity and no overflow.
faults.fix: Classify language and intent. Set overflow when capacity is zero.
faults.check: A test work item in Dynamics with the French billing case.

faults.symptom: CUCM and Teams both rewrite the same number.
faults.cause: Two normalization owners. The hop in the middle sees a number neither side planned.
faults.fix: Pick one system to normalize. The other passes E.164.
faults.check: A ladder with the Request-URI at CUCM, CUBE, and Teams.

faults.symptom: CUBE answers 488 toward Teams.
faults.cause: Early offer was not presented, or the codec intersection is empty.
faults.fix: Send early offer toward Teams and agree a codec both sides list.
faults.check: CUBE SIP trace. Look at SDP on the first INVITE.

faults.symptom: The private CA works in the lab and fails against Teams.
faults.cause: Teams requires a public CA in the Microsoft trusted root program.
faults.fix: Replace the certificate. Do not add your lab root to a fantasy trust store on the Microsoft side.
faults.check: Certificate chain on the SBC.

faults.symptom: Operator Connect numbers fail only for one country.
faults.cause: The operator's coverage and the user's assigned number do not match, or consent was not finished.
faults.fix: Check the operator, the country, and the consent state before you rebuild routes.
faults.check: Operator Connect plan article and the number's operator status.

faults.symptom: Teams Phone Mobile users have no SBC and someone is still designing Direct Routing for them.
faults.cause: Teams Phone Mobile is an operator model. Those users do not need your SBC.
faults.fix: Keep mobile users on the operator. Use Direct Routing only for the population that needs it.
faults.check: The user's phone number type.

faults.symptom: Screen pop opens the wrong CRM contact.
faults.cause: The presented number is not E.164, or the Call-ID was never stored.
faults.fix: Normalize before the pop. Store E.164 and Call-ID on the activity.
faults.check: One test call. Compare the SIP From with the CRM search key.

faults.symptom: WFM says the day was fine and the 10:00 hour missed the target.
faults.cause: The feed is a daily total.
faults.fix: Export queue intervals. Staff the hour, not the average.
faults.check: Interval offered, answered, abandoned, and handle time.

faults.symptom: Power BI and CQD disagree.
faults.cause: The report was built on an export with a different filter, or the subnet map is stale.
faults.fix: Make CQD the source of the quality statement. Refresh the subnet-to-building map before the report.
faults.check: CQD for the building, then the Power BI filter list.

faults.symptom: A user hears voicemail in the wrong language, or not at all.
faults.cause: Cloud Voicemail follows the mailbox. No mailbox, no voicemail.
faults.fix: Confirm the Exchange mailbox and the voicemail policy.
faults.check: Cloud Voicemail article. The user's mailbox.

faults.symptom: The admin center says the SBC is healthy and calls still fail.
faults.cause: Admin center status is not a SIP ladder. OPTIONS can succeed while INVITE fails on a codec or a route.
faults.fix: Take a ladder for the failing Call-ID.
faults.check: SBC trace plus Call Analytics for that call.

faults.symptom: Saturday night the trunk drops and the on-call engineer has no certificate date.
faults.cause: Expiry was not on a shared calendar.
faults.fix: Put certificate and public DNS dates next to the holiday calendar. Renew early.
faults.check: The certificate not-after, and a reminder that is not the SBC itself.

faults.symptom: An interview answer says MS-220 replaced MS-700.
faults.cause: That claim is false. MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026; it is NOT retired and has no replacement.
faults.fix: Read the MS-700 study guide again before you book. Ignore blogs that retire it or name a replacement.
faults.check: Learn certification page for MS-700 and the retirement list.

tips: Confirm the tenant, the verified domain, and the admin role before you touch a voice route.
A resource account is disabled for interactive sign-in. It still needs the license the voice app requires.
Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing can live in one tenant. They are not the same purchase.
traps: Treating a guest, or an admin in the wrong tenant, as if they can grant a voice routing policy.
Opening an SBC ticket when the domain is unverified and the user has no Teams Phone license.
t01.sheet:
Tenant boundary
  Identity   Entra ID user, room, or resource account
  Domain     verified before phone numbers
  Role       Teams administrator, named
  Order      identity, license, policy, then dial tone

tips: Teams Phone lets a user be an enterprise voice user. A Calling Plan is Microsoft acting as the carrier, bought separately.
An auto attendant or call queue resource account usually needs a free virtual-user license, not a Calling Plan, unless that app places outbound calls.
Teams Premium does not include Teams Phone or a phone number.
traps: Buying a Calling Plan and expecting Direct Routing to start working.
Licensing every resource account with a Calling Plan because the queue has a phone number.
t02.sheet:
Teams Phone      user can be enterprise voice
Calling Plan     Microsoft is the PSTN carrier
Operator Connect carrier operates, you assign
Phone Mobile     mobile operator
Direct Routing   you operate the SBC
Resource account its own license, not the agent's
Teams Premium    not a phone system

tips: Read with Get- before you Set- or Grant-.
Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy changes the policy object. Grant-CsTeamsCallingPolicy assigns that policy to a user.
New-CsOnlineVoiceRoute needs a number pattern, an online PSTN gateway, and a PSTN usage, or the route never matches.
traps: Running Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy against a user principal name and thinking the user changed.
Pasting parameters from a screenshot without checking Get-Help in the module installed on that machine.
t03.sheet:
Get-     read
New-     create
Set-     change the object
Grant-   assign to a user
Remove-  delete
Voice route     pattern + gateway + usage
Calling policy  the object. Grant assigns it.

tips: Mark audio EF / DSCP 46, video AF41 / 34, app sharing AF21 / 18, and signaling CS5 / 40. The mark has to survive the trust boundary.
A short path and enough bandwidth beat a clever queue. A VPN is not a media design.
G.711 at 20 ms is about 80 kbit/s at layer 3, and about 87.2 kbit/s with an 18-byte Ethernet header.
traps: Marking DSCP only on the PC and assuming the WAN still honors it.
Treating media bypass as a bandwidth feature. Bypass changes where RTP goes, not the codec math.
t04.sheet:
Audio      DSCP 46  EF
Video      DSCP 34  AF41
Sharing    DSCP 18  AF21
Signaling  DSCP 40  CS5
Confirm the current port ranges on the network article you operate.
VPN pools are a bad place for real-time media.

tips: One user places a call with one connectivity option. The tenant may mix Calling Plan, Operator Connect, Teams Phone Mobile, and Direct Routing.
Direct Routing signaling uses TLS to the Teams SIP proxies on TCP 5061. The SBC FQDN must be in the certificate SAN.
Media bypass can send RTP between the client and the SBC. Signaling stays with Teams.
traps: Using an onmicrosoft.com name, or a sip.pstnhub name, as the SBC FQDN.
Debugging the dial plan when OPTIONS to the trunk are already failing.
t05.sheet:
Proxies   sip, sip2, sip3 .pstnhub.microsoft.com
Signaling TLS 5061
OPTIONS   200 OK or the trunk leaves the route
INVITE    after a voice route picks a gateway
Bypass    RTP may skip the media processor
Signaling does not bypass

tips: Normalization is first match. A later rule does not repair a number an earlier rule already rewrote.
A voice routing policy is an ordered list of PSTN usages. The first usage that contains a matching route wins.
Direct Routing needs the user in TeamsOnly. Islands mode does not send that user's PSTN calls through Teams.
traps: Debugging the gateway when the dialed string never became E.164.
Creating a route and forgetting to put its PSTN usage on the user's policy, in the right order.
t06.sheet:
Dialed string
  -> tenant dial plan, first matching rule
  -> E.164
  -> voice routing policy usages, in order
  -> first voice route regex that matches
  -> online PSTN gateway list
Islands mode does not place Direct Routing calls.

tips: Assign the phone number to the resource account, and assign the resource account to the auto attendant or call queue.
Overflow and timeout need a destination you have already built. A queue that overflows to itself loops.
Attendant routing, serial, round robin, and conference mode are different. Name the one you configured.
traps: Licensing the agents and forgetting the resource account.
Pointing a menu key at a queue that does not exist yet.
t07.sheet:
Resource account -> license -> voice app -> number
Attendant: hours, holidays, menu
Menu key -> person, queue, or another attendant
Queue: agents, presence, method, overflow, timeout
Outbound from the app needs its own calling funding

tips: Dynamic emergency calling walks trusted IP, network site, subnet, and civic address. A VPN pool is often not a dispatchable location.
On Direct Routing you choose whether the SBC or Microsoft routes the emergency call. Say which hop you configured.
A Survivable Branch Appliance keeps a limited set of calls up when the path to Microsoft 365 fails. It does not replace the SBC.
traps: Placing a real emergency call to test a lab. Use the matcher and a test policy.
Treating location-based routing and emergency location as the same feature. They share sites and do different jobs.
t08.sheet:
Trusted IP -> site -> subnet -> civic address
Emergency route: Microsoft or your SBC, on purpose
LBR: selected PSTN stays on the local gateway
SBA: some branch calling during a WAN loss
SBA scope is smaller than normal Teams Phone

tips: Media bypass is a media path. SIP signaling still goes to Teams.
A meeting room has its own license. It does not inherit a person's Calling Plan.
SIP Gateway registers compatible phones to Teams. It is not Direct Routing and it is not your SBC.
traps: Enabling media bypass and expecting AMR-WB. AMR-WB is not negotiated on the bypass path.
Parking a room account on a personal policy with no device account of its own.
t09.sheet:
Processor path   client -> Teams media -> SBC
Bypass path      client -> SBC on the same site
Signaling        always via Teams
AMR-WB           not on bypass
SIP Gateway      phone registration, not a trunk
Room             its own account and SKU

tips: Certification means that SBC software is supported with Direct Routing. You still configure the vendor release you run.
AudioCodes, Ribbon, Oracle, and Cisco CUBE are families. The support path starts with that vendor's guide.
Failover is a second gateway on the voice route that you have rehearsed, not a hostname you hope is warm.
traps: Opening a Microsoft case for a firmware or DSP fault the vendor owns.
Cloning the London trunk to Manchester and leaving the certificate name or the OPTIONS target unchanged.
t10.sheet:
Certified list -> the release you actually run
Pair           primary and secondary, both on the route
Firewall       current Teams ranges, both directions
Rehearse       fail the primary before the site depends on it
Vendor first   when the symptom is on the SBC itself

tips: Use TLS 1.2 or higher, a public CA, and a SAN that matches the SBC FQDN. A name mismatch stops the handshake before INVITE.
OPTIONS from the Teams proxies should receive 200 OK. Missed OPTIONS take the trunk out of service.
AMR-WB is not offered when media bypass is on. The rest of the codec list is a negotiation, not a wish.
traps: Arguing about the dial plan while the certificate is still issued to the old hostname.
Trusting a private CA for Direct Routing. The trunk wants a public certificate.
t11.sheet:
ClientHello -> certificate -> SAN matches FQDN -> Finished
OPTIONS -> 200 OK
INVITE / 100 / 180 / 200 / ACK
RTP follows the SDP: processor or bypass
TCP 5061, not 5060

tips: One call belongs in Call Analytics. A building or a week of calls belongs in the Call Quality Dashboard. The trunk belongs in OPTIONS and the SBC trace.
Write the hypothesis before you change a dial plan. A certificate miss and a bad normalization rule leave different evidence.
A CQD average is not that one user's call. Do not quote it as if it were.
traps: Opening the SBC trace first when Call Analytics already shows the client on a failing Wi-Fi hop.
Calling both Call Analytics and CQD 'the call log.'
t12.sheet:
One user, one call  -> Call Analytics
Many calls, one site -> CQD
Trunk up?           -> SIP OPTIONS
Ladder wrong?       -> SBC syslog
Then change one thing and look again

tips: Dynamics 365 Contact Center is the CCaaS product. AB-250 is the exam that matches it.
AB-210 is the sales successor to MB-280 and is in beta. It does not replace MS-700, and it is not the contact-center exam.
Unified routing uses workstreams, queues, and capacity. A Teams call queue is a different product.
traps: Studying AB-210 because the title says AI when the job is the contact center.
Describing a Teams call queue as unified routing.
t13.sheet:
AB-250 contact center, published ranges
  Deploy            15–20%
  Channels          30–35%
  Agents and AI     10–15%
  Work distribution 10–15%
  Rep experience    15–20%
  Analytics         10–15%
Workstream -> queue -> capacity -> representative

tips: Connect, Extend, and Unify are different media paths. Name the model before you name the product.
CUCM to Teams through Direct Routing is a certified SBC, often CUBE, with one owner for normalization.
Webex, UCCE, Genesys, and Amazon Connect each need a named bridge. 'We integrate' is not a design.
traps: Mapping a CUCM calling search space onto a Teams dial plan as if the objects were the same.
Letting both CUCM and Teams rewrite the same number.
t14.sheet:
Connect  SBC between the PBX and Teams
Extend   Graph and the client; media stays put
Unify    ACS-native contact-center path
CUCM     partition, CSS, route pattern
Teams    dial plan, usage, route, gateway
One system owns normalization

tips: Call Automation is a server-side call: answer, play, recognize, transfer, hang up. Recognize can be DTMF or speech.
Copilot Studio can sit in the recognize step. A transfer to a person is part of the design.
Foundry is where you evaluate a model. It is not a second phone system.
traps: Shipping a bot with no human escape and calling it a contact center.
Assuming speech recognition sees media on a path you never forked.
t15.sheet:
Answer -> Play -> Recognize -> Transfer or Hang up
Recognize   DTMF or speech
Escape      a queue or a person, on every flow
ACS events  are the call
Teams policy is not the bot runtime

tips: MS-700 is still live, with a skills update on Oct 27 2026. It is not retired and it has no replacement.
MB-280 retired Jul 31 2026. AB-210 is its successor and is in beta. AB-210 is the sales exam. It does not replace MS-700.
AB-250 is the contact-center exam. AZ-900 and SC-900 are live. The SC-900 English update is 21 Oct 2026. MS-900 and AI-900 are retired. Renewal is not retirement.
traps: Telling a candidate that AB-210 replaces MS-700.
Booking a retired exam because a blog still lists it as current.
t16.sheet:
MS-700   live; skills update Oct 27 2026; no replacement
AB-250   contact center
AB-210   in beta; successor to MB-280; sales
MB-280   retired Jul 31 2026
AZ-900   live
SC-900   live; English update 21 Oct 2026
MS-900   retired
AI-900   retired
Renewal is not retirement

tips: Compliance recording is a certified recorder, an application instance, an enabled policy, and a grant. The partner stores the media.
Join the logs on an identifier you can name: call id, user, queue, and the recorder's own reference.
The Erlang C calculator in this campus is a teaching model. It is not a workforce-management product.
traps: Expecting a Teams call queue to forecast, score adherence, and run quality management.
Enabling recording without a notice and without granting the policy to the right users.
t17.sheet:
Recording   certified bot, policy, grant, notice
WFM         queue intervals; not a Teams feature
E911        location, then the carrier route
Analytics   CQD, then a model you own, then Power BI
CRM         screen pop on an id you store
Agent       answer, then a human escape

tips: The Dynamics voice channel page says the channel is built on Azure Communication Services. The representative notification it describes is the Copilot Service workspace, not the Teams client.
The Salesforce help page that opened says Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers, formerly Service Cloud Voice, is now part of Partner Contact Center.
traps: Treating a Teams resource account as proof that the representative answers in the Teams client.
Using a remembered application ID. The Teams Phone page prints one. Copy it from the current page.
t18.sheet:
CTI          telephone coordinated with a computer
Dynamics     ACS voice channel, unified routing
Teams number resource account, then Sync from Teams
Calling Plan service numbers only, on that page
Salesforce   Voice, formerly Service Cloud Voice
Record       the id you store, not a matching name

tips: Quote the product name the opened page uses. Amazon’s guide says Amazon Connect Customer is the current name of the product previously called Amazon Connect.
Google’s legal change log records a rename to Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience. The CCAI Platform docs page opened for this track still uses Contact Center AI Platform.
traps: Ranking vendors, or copying a price, a market share, or a certification list this track did not open.
Saying the CCAI Platform docs page was renamed away because a change-log line exists.
t19.sheet:
Microsoft    voice channel, plus Connect Extend Unify
Amazon       Connect Customer, this guide
Google docs  Contact Center AI Platform
Change log   GECX rename is a separate page
No rank      equal bars mean pages opened

tips: Unified routing has two stages on its overview page: classification, then assignment. A voice workstream is push mode only.
A short-term forecast on the forecasting overview is 15-minute intervals for a horizon of up to six weeks (42 days). A long-term forecast is daily, up to three years (1,096 days).
traps: Using a quality score or a forecast for employment decisions. Both pages say not to.
Treating the Dynamics recording announcement and a Teams compliance-recording policy as one switch.
t20.sheet:
Classify    rules and ML models add information
Assign      highest capacity, round robin, least active
Voice queue least active is the default on that page
Forecast    volume and AHT, then capacity, then shifts
Quality     indicators score, guardrails do not
Not for     compensation, seniority, or rewards
